item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02755","case1_error":"Uses 50 total first-day flowers instead of 30 first-day tulips in the tulip sum, double-counting roses.","case2_error":"Confuses elapsed and remaining days, then incorrectly models pill quantities with 6x = 12 + x.","reason":"The first substitutes a combined count for a category count; the second constructs an invalid time-and-dose equation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02756","case1_error":"Subtracts only Ryan’s share, omitting Chris’s required withdrawal.","case2_error":"Divides total area by six as though all rooms were equal; the living room requires three ordinary-room area units.","reason":"Omitting one withdrawal differs from using an unweighted room count despite unequal room sizes.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02757","case1_error":"Omits Ted’s four eaten cookies from the remaining-cookie calculation.","case2_error":"Counts the three cupcakes Sarah gives away as cupcakes she retains, then adds the received cookies.","reason":"The first omits a consumption event; the second substitutes the transferred portion for the retained portion.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02758","case1_error":"Applies the four overtime hours to every working day, multiplying the stated overtime pay by five.","case2_error":"Writes the correct sum 6 + 8 + 4 + 12 but evaluates it as “2L” instead of 30.","reason":"The first incorrectly repeats overtime across days; the second gives an invalid evaluation of a correctly written sum.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02759","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 3,000 × 8 / 6 as 2,000 instead of 4,000.","case2_error":"Provides an unsupported final 34 after correct formulas; the stated savings minus expenses yield 40.","reason":"The first explicitly miscalculates a written expression. The second supplies a wrong final number without showing a numerical evaluation.","judgment":"different"}]}
